spec.title: Casoli and Lucchetti, "Permanent-Transitory decomposition of cointegrated time series via Dynamic Factor Models, with an application to commodity prices" (Econometrics Journal 25(2), 2022): Section 4 commodity application
spec.paper: Chiara Casoli and Riccardo Lucchetti, Permanent-Transitory decomposition of cointegrated time series via Dynamic Factor Models, with an application to commodity prices, The Econometrics Journal 25(2): 494-514, 2022
spec.cost_basis: typical on-demand price for a 4 vCPU, 16 GB cloud machine

setup.cmd: printf 'pkg install DFM\npkg install staticfactor\n' > "$PWD/../pkgs.inp" && gretlcli -b "$PWD/../pkgs.inp"

scope_notes: Section 4 (the commodity application) only. The Monte Carlo in Section 3 has to be edited by hand for each table row (README: set the parameters in `main.inp`, then the file name in `stats.inp`), and its `extra` gretl package could not be downloaded here; it was not run.

The package commits no output files, so there is nothing for the generator to compare. The table printed by `part1.inp` is compared by hand with the paper's cointegration table, as set out in the protocol, and that comparison is listed under notes.
Plots written by `part2.inp` and `part3.inp` are not compared.

commands.cmd: printf 'pkg install DFM\npkg install staticfactor\n' > "$PWD/../pkgs.inp" && gretlcli -b "$PWD/../pkgs.inp"

post_run_notes:
The generator had no committed file to compare, so its own count of reproduced outputs is 0 of 0. The comparison fixed in
the protocol was done by hand, from the `part1.inp` log above against Table 4 (p. 12) of the working paper version
(FEEM Nota di Lavoro 2021-019), not the published article:

| Block | VAR length (paper / run) | Coint. rank (paper / run) | Common trends (paper / run) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base metals | 2 / 2 | 1 / 1 | 5 / 5 |
| Precious metals | 2 / 2 | 1 / 1 | 2 / 2 |
| Energy | 2 / 2 | 3 / 3 | 1 / 1 |
| Livestock | 2 / 2 | 2 / 2 | 4 / 4 |
| Raw materials | 2 / 2 | 1 / 1 | 7 / 7 |
| Food | 2 / 2 | 9 / 9 | 1 / 1 |
| Total | | 17 / 17 | 20 / 20 |

All 20 printed cells match. These are integers chosen by tests (lag length by Hannan-Quinn, rank by the Johansen trace test
at 1%), so a match says the same choices were made here, not that every underlying statistic agrees to many digits.

Reported, not scored: in `part2.log`, the Bai and Ng (2007) criteria suggest q = 1, 2, 2, 1 for the four variants, and
the script takes the largest, 2, which is the q = 2 stated in the paper. The DFM estimation converged by EM in 208
iterations.

`part3.inp` exited 0 but its last command asks gretl to draw a plot on screen, which this headless machine cannot do; the log
shows `Unable to initialize GTK+` there. The numbers it prints before that are in the log and were not compared.
